classification.difficultyReason: Distribute the subtraction over both numerator terms.

answer.short: False. The left-hand side is $\frac{x-3y}{x-y}$, where $x\ne y$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x-y}{x-y}-\frac{x+2y}{x-y}&=\frac{2x-y-(x+2y)}{x-y}\\\frac{2x-y}{x-y}-\frac{x+2y}{x-y}&=\frac{2x-y-x-2y}{x-y}\\\frac{2x-y}{x-y}-\frac{x+2y}{x-y}&=\frac{x-3y}{x-y}\end{align*}$$
Subtract both terms of the second numerator. False as an identity; domain: $x\ne y$.
